what_happened: Both dependency fronts had already landed the two facts this dispatch would otherwise have had to derive: stab_iff_ofut_opast / stab_iff_opast_ofut compile the product factorization of the stability cluster, and paste_valid lands its object-language form (the PS pasting axiom). The automaton verdict could be built on compiled lemmas instead of paper sketches.

PlusLCSchema.lean's module docstring states 'LCU is the n = 1 instance of lcN'. Report 03 section 2.3 defines LCU as the until-form with two parameters and the untl connective; lcN at n=1 is the F-form with one parameter and no untl. The candidate system's until-form ingredient is therefore neither landed nor correctly recorded.

The landed omega_chain dropped the source probe's segment-property parameter P (recorded as 'unused'), but P is exactly the hook report 03 section 2.3 names as LCU's compiled semantic core. The until-form's core is now only in specs/evidence/, not in the library.

Plan phase for a research task whose deliverable (the report) was already complete: the only implementable work left is the dispatch-mandated close-out (amend report 03 section 1.3, file follow-ons R1/R2, summary). Filing follow-on tasks autonomously collides with Multi-Task Creation Standard Component 7, which requires foreground user confirmation; resolved by treating the task description's own 'file the implementation as its own task' as pre-authorization, keeping the full Component 4b audit evidence, and rendering the Component 7 table into the summary as a record rather than prompting. Stated as an assumption in the plan's Risks table, not applied silently.

validate-artifact.sh caught that backticked Verification Tier values (`prose`) do not match its extraction regex, which accepts only a bare word; unbackticking the four values cleared all warnings. Cheap, immediate authoring feedback before the plan left the dispatch.

audit-task-proposals.sh returned a duplicate-of-open verdict for proposal R1 (oriented_forest_saturation) against open task 869 (open_modal_invariance_ray_agreement_lifting), mechanical_class overlap, semantic_score 0.43, shared_paths=[FormalSystem/Semantics/README.md]. Inspection shows the two tasks are unrelated in content (869 is open-future/open-past modal invariance along ray agreement; R1 is an oriented-forest Saturation lemma); the overlap is a single shared low-specificity catch-all README file, not a scope duplication. Disposition: narrowed R1's declared file_scope to drop FormalSystem/Semantics/README.md before filing (keeping only FormalSystem/Semantics/TaskFrame.lean), rather than auto-applying a fold or adding a spurious dependency edge between unrelated tasks.

state-write.sh --audit-verdict FILE fails with exit 126 'Argument list too long' when FILE's largest single NDJSON line exceeds Linux's per-argv MAX_ARG_STRLEN (131072 bytes), because the script slurps the whole file's parsed JSON into one shell variable and passes it to jq via a single --argjson shell argument. This task's audit-task-proposals.sh output had two lines of ~151KB each (dominated by scope-blind verdicts against the ~490 open backlog entries lacking a declared file_scope). Worked around by building a condensed audit-verdict file that keeps every non-scope-blind verdict verbatim and collapses the scope-blind entries into a single count field before passing it to state-write.sh; the full, uncondensed audit file remains committed as the durable evidence. Not fixed here (library/script change is out of scope for this formal/documentation-only task) -- flagged for state-write.sh's own maintainers as a latent size ceiling on --audit-verdict for any backlog audit against a large corpus.
